verdicts.title: Mahler's work on the geometry of numbers
verdicts.abstract_excerpt: Mahler has written many papers on the geometry of numbers. Arguably, his most influential achievements in this area are his compactness theorem for lattices, his work on star bodies and their critical lattices, and his estimates for the successive minima of reciprocal convex bodies and compound convex bodies. We give a, by far not complete, overview of Mahler's work on these topics and their impact.
verdicts.judge_reasoning: The abstract describes Mahler's work on geometry of numbers (compactness theorem, star bodies, successive minima), which shares the name 'Mahler' but does not address Mahler measure of polynomials nor ACC^0[6] circuit complexity.

verdicts.title: Graph complexity and Mahler measure

verdicts.title: Sharp Thresholds Imply Circuit Lower Bounds: from random 2-SAT to Planted Clique
verdicts.abstract_excerpt: We show that sharp thresholds for Boolean functions directly imply average-case circuit lower bounds.
